name: Rubine Red
lede: Rubine Red is a vivid, purplish-red carried in the extended web color lists, its word a spelling of the old French *rubine*, ruby-colored, rather than a name with a documented coiner.

sections.title: A ruby word, an undocumented coining
sections.body:
Our library finds Rubine Red only as a crowd-list entry sourced from Wikipedia, with no first-recorded date and no dictionary, standard or company behind it [1]. The root word, *rubine*, is an old spelling tied to *ruby* and the Latin *rubeus*, red [2]. Wikipedia's own article on the related pigment Lithol Rubine BK, an azo red used in printing, shows the same root turning up as a working name in commercial ink rather than in a paint-chip dictionary [2].

Who attached "rubine" to this particular hex is not recorded in the sources checked here, so the name is treated as undocumented [1]. The nearest color by our look-alike data is [[rose-red|Rose Red]], 2.6 units away and read as a duller version of this red [3], with [[cerise|Cerise]] further off at 5.7, read as lighter.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: At our matching threshold, this exact red does not turn up in any of the 23,781 paintings in the archive, as photographed [4]. That is common for narrow, modern print and web colors: the swatch sits in a band of saturated red-violet that period paintings rarely reproduce this precisely, and the absence is a gap in the match, not evidence the color never appears in art [4]. Measured, Rubine Red comes out at lightness 45, chroma 73, hue 11 degrees, decisively more purple than a plain fire-engine red [4].
